rows.basis: The FY2026 MD&A credits the 12% revenue rise and the 12% Semiconductor Process Control rise to leading-edge foundry/logic, memory and advanced-packaging investment 'supported by strong demand associated with AI and HPC applications'. It gives no figure. Semiconductor Process Control ($12,244,733,000 of $13,579,476,000) is an end market broader than AI and is not used as a segment. The roughly $1.1bn calendar-2026 advanced-packaging outlook is not in the pack.

The FY2025 MD&A credits the 24% revenue rise to leading-edge foundry investment 'driven by the AI infrastructure buildout' and to adoption of the advanced-packaging portfolio. It gives no AI or advanced-packaging figure. Semiconductor Process Control ($10,947,359,000) is broader than AI.

Capex of $375,945,000 goes to KLA's own factories, labs and R&D sites, and no AI part of it is stated. The seller-side signal is AI named qualitatively as a driver of FY2026 revenue (Semiconductor Process Control $12,244,733,000); that is not KLA's AI spend.
Capex of $335,259,000 has no stated AI part. The seller-side signal, the AI infrastructure buildout named as a FY2025 revenue driver, is a demand statement and not KLA's spend.
Capex of $277,384,000 has no stated AI part and no AI revenue statement for the year.
Capex of $341,591,000 has no stated AI part and no AI revenue statement for the year.
Capex of $307,320,000 has no stated AI part and no AI revenue statement for the year.
